text: Everyone has an explanation and leadership has the cost case. Now we write the document for the engineering record: a real after-action report, built like a blameless postmortem.

The timeline: harvest traffic scales the autoscaler to fourteen replicas, all healthy. About eighteen minutes later, the dashboard flags cost climbing while database load stays flat. Fixed by roughly the forty-minute mark.

Root cause, stated plainly: a security rule used a label that had never matched this service's pods since the day it was applied, weeks before harvest. It stayed invisible until real traffic made it matter.
What went right: a cost-hygiene dashboard caught it anyway. What went wrong: two sources of truth for one label, and no check that tested the connection that actually mattered.
Four follow-ups, each owned and dated -- three already complete. Up next: the series finale.
